standard.title: Integers: Compare, Order, Add and Subtract
standard.description: compare, order and solve problems involving addition and subtraction of integers
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can locate integers on a number line and recognise negative integers in context (from AC9M6N01). Students understand magnitude and direction in simple contexts (above/below zero, gain/loss).
standard.progression_endpoint: Students compare and order integers using inequality notation and solve problems involving addition and subtraction of integers.

nodes.label: Comparing and ordering integers
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students compare and order integers using less-than and greater-than notation, including negative integers.
nodes.minimum_width: Order a given set of integers (including negatives) from least to greatest and use <, > notation to compare pairs.
nodes.typical_width: Place a mixed set of integers on a number line; use inequality notation in expressions; explain why −7 < −2.
wider: Investigate absolute value informally: distance from zero on a number line. Compare |−7| and |2| without formal notation.
Connect ordering to real contexts: temperature below zero, sea level, financial debt.

response_modes.reason: Students commonly believe −7 > −2 because 7 > 2. Multiple real-world contexts (temperature, floors below ground, financial loss) help resolve the magnitude vs direction confusion.

nodes.hinge_reason: The magnitude-vs-direction confusion (believing −7 > −2) produces systematic errors in Node 2 addition and subtraction — students who cannot correctly order integers cannot set up or check integer calculations.
success_criteria: Correctly orders a set of integers including negatives.
Uses < and > notation correctly between integers.
Does not confuse the magnitude of a negative with its value (e.g. understands −10 < −1).

nodes.label: Addition and subtraction of integers
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students add and subtract integers using a number line and understand the effect of adding or subtracting a negative number.
nodes.minimum_width: Calculate simple integer additions and subtractions using a number line (e.g. −3 + 5, 4 − 7, −2 − 3).
nodes.typical_width: Calculate integer sums and differences without a number line; interpret addition of a negative and subtraction of a negative; apply in context.
wider: Investigate the pattern: subtracting a negative equals adding a positive — explain using number line movement.
Explore temperature change problems requiring chaining multiple integer additions and subtractions.

response_modes.reason: Integer addition and subtraction is a major misconception site. Students confuse the sign of the number with the operation sign. Number line contexts, thermometer contexts, and financial contexts each address different facets of the misconception.

The rule 'subtract a negative = add a positive' requires explicit reasoning: movement on a number line combined with meaning of the operation. Without scaffolding, students apply rules inconsistently.

nodes.hinge_reason: The operation-sign/number-sign confusion produces persistent errors in AC9M7N06 rational number operations and AC9M7N09 modelling contexts — students who cannot confidently add and subtract integers cannot handle any signed number computation downstream.
success_criteria: Correctly adds and subtracts integers including cases with negative operands.
Interprets adding a negative number as movement in the negative direction.
Does not treat subtraction of a negative as subtraction (e.g. 5 − (−3) = 8, not 2).
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The pattern that subtracting a negative equals adding a positive, explained through number line movement, is a rich structural insight — advancing students can use this to reason about multi-step integer expressions.
